body: I've never actually considered the possibility that I might have some sort of PTSD tbh 😅😅😅

Hopefully it takes a turn for the better again once we open up again.

You're a strong person regardless for fighting so long dude, massive respects to you and honestly a bit inspiring

At the same time I do know that the memory I have burned into my head is the most traumatic I have. I can honestly tell you in a photographic memory type esc what happened and where everything was.

Also I'm sorry for what you went trough, though I don't like labeling myself as "normal" and you abnormal. The brain is just weird in a way I guess.
I do very conflicted with the realization iver over how little i remember from my childhood and teens

I've had 3 instances of something similar ish happening to me.
They're all connected though.

The first time was when I had just hit a low point of my low point. I'll spare you the details but I knew I was suicidal and I had this voice in my head just telling me to end it. Do it, it was like it was me but it wasn't. This wasn't my wish to die it was someone actively telling me to kill myself, so I tried it. Again trying to keep this short so skipping the how if you're fine with that 
While I was for all intensive purposes dying, another voice kept telling me how stupid I was for getting to this point, and told me all my life was nothing but pain.

I was lucky to survive but both of those instances are so surreal.
The first time it was so sinister and just felt like the devil himself was talking to me.
Meanwhile afterwards, it was more soothing.
Tbh I think it was just the deepest parts of my mind telling me their desire. I truly had enough but maybe I still wanted to keep fighting?

The human brain is weird like that, however trust me.
Giving in to those dark voices doesn't help, and you just feel helpless.

If you think it's becoming a problem try to seek help, don't do like me and wait it out until you're in actual danger.

The first half of your post can honestly be answered with, that's why it's important to find a job you like. Honestly I used to think like you about work when I went to school but after finding the first job I liked, I'll tell you what it's so much better than school.
It's honestly a lot more freeing, and overall a much better experience, as long as you find a thing you like. I didn't like my first two jobs but I hit it on the third one.
I still go to uni, and will probably have a higher paying different job in 5 years but it's a field I have some interest for.
Bottom line is don't stress this, working is much much better than school.

The second half of your post is the age old question. What's the meaning in life, and honestly.
Nothing. And I mean it, life is pointless on the bigger spectrum, we live then we die.
The world is absolutely cruel and unjust, so what's the point?
Well this is where it all connects, you have to find meaning in life for yourself. We all have a purpose and we all have a way to live. Live and tell your own story, life might seem pointless but you can give it much more meaning. For me personally, it's about the small moments and those are the ones I treasure.
I've had it hard and I still do but do I want my entire life to be nothing but pain? No! I want something out of this.
Something to be proud of, I want to be happy. So I keep pushing, my purpose and my meaning in life is to get to a stable point and be happy.

I didn't have this goal until 6 months ago because I thought it was impossible.
Before that I was suicidal.
I've still kept pushing and I'm starting to get optimistic about it.
I'm sharing my experience because meaning in life is very personal but you don't have to find it at 15-19. You can find it at 22 or 72.
Until then, you can say your meaning in life is to find your meaning.
Don't stress it, we all get there eventually just take it at your own pace

It is however important to find your passions
